description.narrative:
International impact. Strengthen political advocacy, knowledge generation, and strategic alliances with and among civil society organizations (CSOs) from the Global South to achieve a fair, transparent, inclusive, gender-just and environmentally friendly international tax system that promotes financial integrity and enables the equitable mobilization of resources for sustainable development.
Country level impact Strengthened and coordinated civil society actors, as well as well-informed and critical journalists, promote fiscal systems in developing countries to be increasingly sovereign, progressive, effective and transparent, and serve to reduce inequalities, including gender-inequalities, as well as promote economic, environmental and social justice and enable progress toward the 2030 Agenda.
Outputs. 1) 300 CSOs in minimum 45 developing countries of them minimum 15 Sub Saharan African countries, including Malawi, Mozambique, Ghana, Sierra Leone and Nigeria, promote public discourse and solutions on domestic resource mobilization (DRM), economic justice, transparency and financial integrity. 2) Minimum 175 CSOs in 60 developing countries, of which minimum 25 are from Sub-Saharan Africa, engage with and influence global processes related to public finance and financial integrity, including the UN Tax Convention process and follow-up to the 4th Financing for Development (FfD) Conference. 3) 320 journalists from 42 developing countries have greater capacity to investigate and report on taxation, financial secrecy and illicit financial flows (IFF), including tax evasion, tax avoidance and
